To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
calpain-catalyzed proteolysis of dUTPases specifically removes the nuclear localization signal peptide.
calpain cleavage of human DUTPase removes the N-terminal nuclear localization peptide, and that the catalytic activity of dUTP is unaffected by calpain proteolysis.

Ca2+-m-calpain proteolysis of dUTP, the essential human enzyme that prevents the incorporation of uracil instead of thymidine during DNA synthesis, results in removal of the N-terminal peptide that contains the nuclear localization signal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the cleavage sites and functional significance of Ca2+-calpaing-mediated proteolysis of dUTPases.
the potential functional significance of Ca2+-calpin-induced proteolysis of dUTPases.
the structural/functional consequences of Ca2+-calpin-induced cleavage of dUTPases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
calpain cleavage of dUTP is an important regulatory step for dUTPase activity and function.
calpain proteolysis of dUTPases may serve to modulate the cellular levels of dUTP and/or dUTPase in a cell type- and developmental stage-dependent manner.
calpain-catalyzed cleavage of human DUTPase removes a nuclear targeting signal peptide, which may regulate dUTPase availability and/or degradation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Ca2+-activated m-calpain proteolysis of dUTPases from both human and Drosophila is a conserved event and the cleavage sites are also conserved, suggesting an important role for calpain-mediated proteolysis of this enzyme in both organisms.
the N-terminal nuclear localization sequence of human dUTPsae is removed by Ca(II)-calpain proteolysis, which may be a mechanism of regulation of dUTPse nuclear availability.
Ca2+-dependent calpain proteases are capable of cleaving dUTPase at specific peptide bonds to produce fragments that are devoid of the N-terminal nuclear localization peptide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calpain-catalyzed proteolysis of dUTPases is a conserved process, with implications in the regulation of dUTP metabolism in eukaryotes.
calpain-mediated cleavage of dUTPases is a conserved process, which may play a significant role in the regulation of dUTP metabolism and genomic integrity.
the nuclear availability of dUTPases is regulated by calpains, and this may have implications in cancer and other diseases.
